text: Triangles which are on equal bases and between the same parallels are equal to one another. Let $ABC$ and $DEF$ be triangles on the equal bases $BC$ and $EF$, and between the same parallels $BF$ and $AD$. I say that triangle $ABC$ is equal to triangle $DEF$.
For let $AD$ have been produced in both directions to $G$ and $H$,
and let the (straight-line) $BG$ have been drawn through $B$ parallel to $CA$ [Prop.~1.31],
and let the (straight-line) $FH$ have been drawn through $F$ parallel to $DE$ [Prop.~1.31].

assertion: GBCA and DEFH are each parallelograms

text: And $GBCA$ is equal to $DEFH$. For they are on the equal bases $BC$ and $EF$, and between  the same parallels $BF$ and $GH$ [Prop.~1.36].

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: they are on the equal bases $BC$ and $EF$, and between  the same parallels $BF$ and $GH$

text: And triangle $ABC$ is half of the parallelogram $GBCA$. For the diagonal $AB$ cuts the latter in half [Prop.~1.34].
assertion: triangle ABC is half of parallelogram GBCA

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: triangle $ABC$ is half of the parallelogram $GBCA$

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the diagonal $AB$ cuts the latter in half

text: And triangle $FED$ (is) half of parallelogram $DEFH$. For the diagonal $DF$ cuts the latter in half.
assertion: triangle FED is half of parallelogram DEFH

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the diagonal $DF$ cuts the latter in half

text: [And the halves of equal things are equal to one another.]
assertion: the halves of equal things are equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the halves of equal things are equal to one another

text: Thus, triangle $ABC$ is equal to triangle $DEF$.
assertion: triangle ABC is equal to triangle DEF

text: Thus, triangles which are on equal bases and between the same parallels are equal to one another. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
